conventions.convention: Exact finite-regulator observables are specified Hermitian matrices on C^d, d ≥ 1. Formal coefficient records have no evaluation or probability interpretation without separate justification and adoption; empirical estimates retain source conditions and uncertainty.

Energy matrices are in joules, time is in seconds, ħ is in joule-seconds, and λ is dimensionless. The Hilbert pairing is first-variable-linear; coordinate contractions use the explicitly distinguished second-variable-linear convention.

Probability claims assume Countable Choice, a unit initial vector, an explicitly supplied orthogonal projective resolution of the identity, adopted pure-state evolution by the constructed U, and the constructed-model Born interpretation.

The oscillator uses positive mass and frequency, the finite Hermite span as an invariant domain, X(t)=U(t)*XU(t), and time ordering with X(t)X(0) for t ≥ 0 and X(0)X(t) for t < 0. Its kernels are C_F(t)=exp(-iω|t|)/(2ω) and G_R(t)=1_[0,∞)(t)sin(ωt)/ω.

load_bearing.statement: A formal coefficient record is a sequence of specified coefficients; without separately proved convergence and an evaluation map, its displayed series is not an evaluated function, exact probability, convergent perturbation series, or error bound. Empirical estimates retain their reported uncertainty and conditions.

Under Countable Choice, the stated finite Hermitian Hamiltonian data, unit-vector preparation, supplied projective measurement and adopted model update/Born interpretation, p_a=||P_aU(τ)ψ||² lies in [0,1], Σ_a p_a=1, and |p_a-q_a,N| ≤ (2√q_a,N+R_N)R_N, where q_a,N=||P_aU_N(τ)ψ||² and R_N=e^z z^(N+1)/(N+1)!. The item also states finite-unitarity coefficient identities, the two-level quartic error bound, nonexponential survival, and the occupation-truncation commutator.

concerns.concern: The Statement follows its projective-measurement identities with “Equivalently, the one-Kraus-per-outcome data M_{a,1}=P_a form a normalized finite instrument”. Normalization alone does not characterize a projective measurement: P_1=P_2=I/√2 gives a normalized one-Kraus-per-outcome instrument but neither operator is a projection. The earlier explicit projection hypotheses and the proof are sound; the equivalence wording should express only their implication to instrument normalization.

alerts.finding: The Setup distinguishes the gyromagnetic ratio from “the QFT coupling g_em in [[def-qft-example-observable-types]]”. That Definition names the dimensionless coupling g, not g_em. The distinction between coupling and gyromagnetic factor is correct, but this exact symbol attribution does not match its cited definition.

seams_checked.note: The unit dictionary and constructed-model Born postulate are used with supplied state/instrument data, Countable Choice and an explicit adopted state update. No apparatus realization or continuum existence is inferred.

Checked finite-Dyson hypotheses and remainder, finite coefficient identities, two-level and occupation-truncation calculations, and the oscillator kernel conventions against their suppliers. Consumer calculations preserve their finite/one-mode scope.

The formal-observable adoption and the scattering/Dirac items preserve the distinction between formal coefficients, exact constructed-model quantities and empirical estimates. They do not use the finite probability theorem as a continuum scattering justification.

This is a contextual page prerequisite; the count theorem does not directly invoke either qft-x01 item. Its physical reading uses the separately constructed free coherent state, count PVM and finite Born instruments, without extending the finite-dimensional theorem to Fock space.
